MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Child and Family Remote Support Worker | Remote Area Family Service | Emerald 

Employment Term: Maximum Term to end of December 2026, Full Time (76 hours per fortnight)

Located in: Emerald 

Remuneration: $44.58 p-h + Super + $15,900 NFP Salary Packaging

Applications Close: Applications will be reviewed as they are received and therefore may result in the role closing early if the right applicant is found.

Make a meaningful difference with UnitingCare

At UnitingCare we are leaders in crisis response, the protection of vulnerable people and children, financial resilience and family wellbeing. Our FaDS (Family and Disability Services) team work passionately across Queensland to make a meaningful difference in people's lives.

As a Child and Family Remote Support Worker, you'll be encouraged to grow, develop and feel empowered to make the everyday easier for the people we care so passionately about. Let's make a meaningful difference, together!

Your part in our UnitingCare team

Our Remote Area Families Service (RAFS) program is seeking a passionate and autonomous worker to join our Remote Area Child and Family Services Team, servicing Emerald and surrounding areas. In joining the team, you will be working alongside fellow RAFS workers located in Mt Isa, Charleville, Mareeba and Longreach.

Your commitment to the role will explore the dynamics of working with our vulnerable clients in communities focusing on:

Supporting early childhood development, parenting resilience and mobile services to communities.

Develop and implement programs to strengthen family relationships, implement early intervention and prevention activities.

Enhance and support increased First Nations- Multicultural community participation and family functioning.

Providing information, advice and referral pathways.

Increase awareness of children's wellbeing and adopt a holistic approach to supporting early childhood education, aligning with family and child support to nurture children and prepare them fully for learning and life.

Understanding the role is predominantly delivered in remote locations and resulting in approximately 60% of work hours spent travelling and overnighting in communities.

This is a unique opportunity to explore the rural and remote outback of Queensland while visiting children and families on stations, in communities, and learning about rural life and working with stakeholders who are committed to supporting families and children to reach their best outcomes.

What makes a difference for us? 

A Tertiary Qualification or working towards Diploma or higher in Children's Services, Counselling, Community Services or relevant field

Be a highly motivated and energetic person who has demonstrated experience working with young children and their development, supporting families and communities

Current Queensland driver's license

Blue Card

What makes a difference for you?

Flexible work arrangements to support work-life balance 

NFP Salary Packaging: Save tax and increase your take home pay by salary packaging your everyday living expenses and bills (up to $15,900) and meal entertainment (up to $2,650) per annum. To learn more about this benefit watch the video via the following link: Salary Packaging Explained 

A recognition and rewards platform, providing employee discounts at hundreds of retailers, including everyday expenses, holidays, health insurance, annual awards celebration, wellbeing and employee assistance programs 

12 weeks paid parental leave and 2 weeks paid partner leave, available after 6 months service, in addition to the government scheme 

Diversity and inclusive leave, offering paid gender affirmation leave and cultural leave options (paid and unpaid) for those who may celebrate Lunar New Year, Diwali, Ramadan, NAIDOC weeks and other significant cultural events 

Career development opportunities to challenge yourself, grow and make a meaningful difference 

A positive and inclusive team based on respect, shared standards, strong values and a commitment to serving others 

We'd love you to be part of our UnitingCare family 

Joining our FaDS, team, you'll also be welcomed as part of the UnitingCare family. The second-largest Queensland employer, we're a proud not-for-profit with more than 16,500 staff and 9,000 volunteers across our brands of BlueCare, Lifeline, ARRCS, The Wesley Hospital, Buderim Private Hospital, St Stephen's Hospital, and St Andrew's War Memorial Hospital, and have been leading by example for more than 100 years. 

Child safe, Child friendly 

UnitingCare is committed to being a Child Safe, Child Friendly organisation and will: 

provide welcoming, safe and nurturing services for children 

implement measures to prevent child abuse and neglect within our services 

appropriately and immediately address child abuse and neglect if it does occur 

abide by the Child Safe Standards and adhere to the Reportable Conduct Scheme 

Diversity & Inclusion 

Our approach is simple - everybody is welcome here. At UnitingCare, diversity is at the core of our who we are, our mission and our values. We are committed to providing equal opportunities to all employees no matter their sex, race, culture, sexual orientation, disability or gender identity. Demonstrating our commitment to reconciliation and building long-term employment opportunities for First Nations peoples, UnitingCare strongly encourages Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants for this position. 

Safe workplace 

We work hard to make our services welcoming and safe for every person. We are united in keeping children, young people and the elderly safe from harm, within our services, workplaces and the communities we support. We are committed to speaking up loudly for their safety. 

Commitment to Safeguarding

We are committed in creating services and workplaces that are welcoming and safe for every person. We work together to protect children, young people, adults and the elderly from harm within our services and the communities we support. We speak up for their safety to ensure their voices are heard. Our recruitment and workplace practices reflect our dedication in preventing abuse, harm and exploitation across UnitingCare.    Click here to Apply now →

result.description:
The Client  

Maidstone Smash Repairs is an automotive service and repair workshop based in Maidstone, VIC, specialising in vehicle diagnostics, mechanical repairs, and routine servicing. The business supports a broad client base by delivering reliable automotive solutions, ensuring vehicles operate safely, efficiently, and in line with manufacturer and regulatory standards. 

They are seeking an experienced Motor Mechanic to join their team in Maidstone, VIC. 

 

 

The Role 

The Motor Mechanic is responsible for delivering diagnostic, repair, and maintenance services across a range of vehicles, ensuring all work meets technical specifications, safety standards, and customer requirements. 

This is a full-time position with an annual salary of $82,500 plus superannuation.  

 

The Responsibilities 

Diagnose mechanical and electrical faults using diagnostic tools, testing equipment, and technical procedures 

Inspect vehicles and assess system performance across engines, transmissions, suspension, steering, and braking systems 

Perform servicing and maintenance tasks including oil changes, brake servicing, and system adjustments 

Dismantle, repair, and reassemble engine components, transmissions, and associated mechanical systems 

Replace defective parts and components in accordance with manufacturer specifications and repair standards 

Conduct testing and verification of repairs to ensure functionality, safety, and compliance 

Interpret technical manuals, service documentation, and repair guides to support accurate diagnostics and repairs 

Maintain records of servicing, repairs, and parts usage in line with workshop and compliance requirements 

Identify additional faults or service requirements and communicate findings to supervisors or customers 

Ensure all work is completed in accordance with workplace safety procedures and automotive standards 

Maintain workshop tools, equipment, and work areas in safe and operational condition 

Coordinate with team members to ensure efficient workflow and timely completion of jobs 

 

 

The Requirements:	 

Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology or equivalent qualification 

AQF Certificate III & IV in a related Motor Mechanic field 

At least 15 months of motor mechanical experience in a commercial workshop setting 

At least 15 months’ experience diagnosing mechanical and electrical faults across vehicle systems 

Minimum 15 months’ experience performing servicing, maintenance, and repair of engines, transmissions, and braking systems 

Must have at least 15 months experience working with Intercontinental, Asian and European car vehicles 

Must have at least 15 months motor mechanical experience with diesels, AWDs, 4WDs, 

Must have at least 15 months experience with EV and Hybrid vehicles 

Ability to interpret technical manuals, specifications, and repair documentation 

Strong problem-solving skills and ability to identify and resolve mechanical issues efficiently 

Good understanding of workplace safety procedures and automotive compliance standards 

Ability to work independently and manage workload in a workshop environment 

Good communication skills and ability to liaise with team members and customers 

Valid Driver’s Licence

OFFICE MANAGER (ANZSCO 512111)
Full-Time | Adelaide, South Australia
Salary: $75,000 – $95,000 + Superannuation

About Bide With Care Pty Ltd
Bide With Care Pty Ltd (BWC) is a registered NDIS provider committed to delivering high-quality disability and aged care support services across South Australia. We provide person-centred care tailored to participant goals, independence, dignity, and wellbeing.
Our services include disability support, community participation, in-home care, personal care, supported accommodation, and aged care services. Due to continued business growth and increasing operational demands, we are seeking an experienced and highly organised Office Manager to oversee our office administration, operational systems, compliance functions, and staff coordination.

About the Role
The Office Manager is responsible for organising and controlling the administrative functions and resources of the office, including office systems, administrative staff, operational workflows, compliance systems, and business support functions.
This role plays a critical leadership function in ensuring efficient daily operations, regulatory compliance, workforce coordination, and continuous business improvement.

Key Responsibilities
Office Operations & Service Planning
•	Oversee daily office operations and administration functions to ensure smooth and efficient service delivery.
•	Contribute to the planning and review of office services, priorities, and service standards.
•	Develop, implement, and improve administrative systems, workflows, and reporting structures.
•	Drive accountability, workflow visibility, and operational efficiencies.
Resource Allocation & Staff Coordination
•	Allocate human resources, office space, equipment, and operational resources effectively.
•	Assign work to administrative staff and monitor work performance.
•	Coordinate operational communication between support workers, coordinators, nurses, and management.
•	Support workforce planning, scheduling, and resource allocation.
Compliance & Records Management
•	Manage company records, participant documentation, and office filing systems.
•	Maintain service agreements, incident reports, risk assessments, compliance registers, and internal records.
•	Ensure documentation complies with NDIS Practice Standards and Quality & Safeguards requirements.
•	Support preparation for audits, regulatory reporting, and compliance reviews.
Financial & Accounts Administration
•	Assist with accounts payable and receivable functions.
•	Manage invoices, purchase orders, reconciliations, and payment processing.
•	Assist with payroll coordination and financial administration.
•	Support budgeting and expenditure monitoring.
Operational Liaison & Problem Resolution
•	Liaise with healthcare professionals, participants, families, and external stakeholders to coordinate business operations.
•	Facilitate prompt resolution of operational, compliance, and administrative issues.
•	Support management with business planning and operational improvement initiatives.
Human Resources Coordination
•	Coordinate onboarding, recruitment support, staff induction, and compliance documentation.
•	Maintain HR records, staff training registers, and performance documentation.
•	Assist with personnel activities including hiring, performance management, payroll coordination, and supervision.
WHS & Legislative Compliance
•	Ensure compliance with occupational health and safety regulations.
•	Maintain workplace safety records and risk management systems.
•	Ensure operations comply with relevant legislation, government regulations, and internal policies.

Essential Skills & Experience
•	Diploma, Advanced Diploma, Associate Degree or higher in Business Administration, Management, Office Administration, or related field.
OR
•	Minimum three years’ relevant experience in office management or business administration.
•	Strong leadership and organisational skills.
•	Demonstrated experience managing office systems and administration functions.
•	Experience managing records, compliance systems, and operational workflows.
•	Strong financial administration and reporting capability.
•	Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and problem-solving skills.

Desirable
•	Experience in disability services, aged care, healthcare, or community services.
•	Knowledge of NDIS compliance and regulatory frameworks.
•	Experience in rostering and workforce coordination.

Why Join BWC?
•	Work with a growing and reputable NDIS provider.
•	Join a supportive and purpose-driven team.
•	Opportunity to contribute to meaningful outcomes for participants.
•	Leadership role with career growth opportunities.
If you are a highly motivated and experienced professional looking to contribute to operational excellence in a growing care organisation, we encourage you to apply.

  About Joii: 
Joii undertakes various trade work for businesses throughout Queensland. By taking up a position with Joii it means that you are part of a bigger family and have access to a range of opportunities with a number of businesses. You also get the added bonus that what you do will make a difference in the community.

Our clients are some of Australia’s biggest and strong demand will ensure long-term employment.
We believe in Creating Opportunity and any profits we create do exactly that for those who need a little bit of extra support.

Joii provides hope and opportunity for disadvantaged and vulnerable people. Joii's approach is twofold:
•	We provide social impact programs that offer hope and opportunity for the disadvantaged and vulnerable. The programs focus on providing employment, pathways to employment, and housing opportunities.
•	We operate sustainable funding creating social enterprises whose objective is to support the vision.

The Opportunity:
Joii offers secure, well-paid positions with the added bonus that what you do will make a difference in our community. 

Due to a long, strong, and ongoing pipeline of work we are ungently seeking enthusiastic and motivated applicants for the positions of qualified Motor Mechanic within our Queensland Trades Team who will work for our valued clients. 

Essential skills needed:
•	Qualification or 3+ years’ experience in floor finishing
•	Expertise knowledge of current flooring requirements;
•	Ability to manage own time and others to meet agreed timeframe and projects:
•	Able to work on tasks autonomously;
•	Construction OHS card (white card) (we will help you obtain this);
•	Supply & maintain own commercial grade tools, noting a tool maintenance allowance is included in the salary package) 
•	Provide own vehicle to get themselves and their tools to site. 
•	Maintain current driver’s license;

About You:
•	Able to work unsupervised and part of a team;
•	Able to follow instructions;
•	Hard working and reliable;
•	Attention to detail and able to work to deadlines.

What you need to do now
If you are interested and have the experience, we would love to hear from you!
Please click the 'APPLY' button now and send through your resume and cover letter detailing your previous relevant experience and why you are the perfect candidate for our team.
Please note, due to the high number of applications we expect to receive, we will only be responding to applicants who have been successful in securing an interview.
Additional Information:
AQF Certificate III including at least two years of on-the-job training, or AQF Certificate IV (ANZSCO Skill Level 3)
The role is for an all-round flooring installer that can complete work to Australian Standards and measures, cuts, installs and repairs carpet, timber, vinyl, resilient resin and concrete floor coverings.
Tasks include: 
•	measuring areas to be covered and consulting plans to estimate quantities of floor covering materials required
•	preparing surfaces for covering and removing baseboard trims
•	measuring, cutting and fixing underlay materials
•	laying coverings, such as carpets, linoleum, parquetry blocks, cork tiles and other resilient flooring
•	materials, over floors, matching patterns, cutting shapes around fixtures and trimming edges
•	securing floor coverings and fitting edge trims in doorways
•	sanding, staining and applying finishing coatings to timber floors
•	may install wall, ceiling, counter and bench coverings

 Department of Health

 Applications must be submitted by Sunday 26 July, 2026 11:55 PM 




Position details

Region:

 
South

 

 

Located in:

4-22 Elizabeth St, Hobart


 

 
Job description:

 
Shape better outcomes for Tasmanians. Join the Department of Health and drive funding, policy and projects that make a real impact.

 

 






 

The Team

System Management and Reform (SMR) is the central policy, strategy, and planning group for the Department of Health (DoH). Strategic Purchasing and Funding (SPF) is a unit within SMR that manages and undertakes a lead role in the purchasing of services within the public and private sectors that drive high quality, value for money outcomes for Tasmanians, and monitoring the delivery of those services by providers to ensure key outcomes are achieved.

The Role

Contribute significantly to the efficient and effective operation of the SPF Unit in the development, implementation and monitoring of funding agreements, contracts of services, policies and procedures.
Undertake a diverse range of project related activities relating to commissioning, policy, procedural, and administrative frameworks.

You will need

Provide high level analysis of current commissioning frameworks to ensure consistency and currency, supporting the review, reform and improvement of operations and services.

Undertake qualitative and quantitative research, including collecting, analysing, and interpreting data and preparing reports, maintaining accurate and comprehensive record keeping systems that support continuous improvement and service delivery.

Coordinate and manage project-related work, liaising with stakeholders and providing advice and innovative options for consideration on matters relating to commissioning frameworks, including systems, policies and procedures.

Review and provide specialist advice on commissioning frameworks, recommending continuous improvement strategies and developing supporting documentation and guidelines as required.

Note: - Please refer to the Statement of Duties for all the selection criteria of this position to address in your application.

Why Tasmania

The Department of Health Tasmania oversees various hospitals across the state, including the Royal Hobart Hospital, Launceston General Hospital, Northwest Regional Hospital, and Mersey Community Hospital, as well as district hospitals and ambulance services. Additionally, it provides community health, mental health, and primary healthcare services to the Tasmanian community through more than 300 sites.

Tasmania, Australia's only island state, offers unparalleled natural beauty and a luxurious lifestyle. Pursuing your health career in Tasmania's public health system means building strong connections with colleagues and patients. It also means embracing a lifestyle where you can enjoy extraordinary experiences outside of work while making a significant impact on the community during work.

Details of appointment

Permanent full time, day worker position, working 76 hours per fortnight, commencing as soon as possible.

*Notwithstanding hours to be negotiated with the successful applicant.

Applicants should note that, for a period of twelve months from the date of publication, this selection process may be used to fill subsequent or similar full time, part time, and casual vacancies.

Salary

$102,027 to $106,985 per annum. Our Employer 12% superannuation contribution is on top of this amount.

Salary range is in accordance with Public Sector Unions Wages Agreement 2025.

Benefits available to eligible candidates

A range of leave entitlements, including study leave and Professional Development Support.

Fitness Passport - You, and your family can access 40+ fitness facilities across Tasmania for just $14.50 per week per person, or $28.05 for a family.

More information about our Employee Benefits can be found here

Eligibility

Applicants should note the following criteria are desirable:

Relevant qualification from a recognised institution or equivalent experience

Position Features

Some intrastate travel may be required

REDEEM SKILLS RECRUITMENT SOLUTIONS (RECRUITER) on behalf of JP Dhiman Pty Ltd trading as EasAbility Care Australia, Fullarton, South Australia 5063

About Company 
JP Dhiman Pty Ltd trading as EasAbility Care Australia is a NDIS-registered disability support provider in South Australia delivering high-quality, person-centred services across. Company support participants to live independently and engage meaningfully in their communities through tailored care and support. Our team is committed to respect, inclusion, and empowering individuals to achieve their goals in a safe and supportive environment. Company offers a generous salary, flexible shifts (Morning, Afternoon, and Night), ongoing professional development, growth opportunities, and a supportive team environment. Positions are available in Adelaide and surrounding areas. 

About the Role: 
As an Aged/Disability Support Worker, you will play a crucial role in assisting our participants to live life to the fullest. You will deliver high-quality care within clients' homes and EasAbility SIL homes, ensuring their holistic needs are met. In this integrated team position, you will work within an established framework to support clients in achieving choice, control, and independence in all aspects of their lives. Your responsibilities will include providing personal care, meal preparation, maintaining the home environment, facilitating community access, and promoting overall well-being. 

Key Responsibilities: 
1. Personal Care: Assisting clients with personal hygiene, dressing and grooming. 
2. Medication Management: Administering medications and ensuring compliance with prescribed treatments. 
3. Daily Living Assistance: Helping with household chores, meal preparation, and shopping. 
4. Mobility Support: Assisting with mobility and transportation to appointments and social activities, 
5. Emotional Support: Providing companionship and engaging in meaningful activities. 
6. Health Monitoring: Observing and reporting any changes in clients’ health or behavior. 
7. Documentation: Maintaining accurate records of care provided and clients’ progress. 

Required Skills and Qualifications: 

•	Certificate III or higher qualifications in Individual Support (Aged Care or Disability) or equivalent. 
•	Experience: 12 months of work experience (full time, part-time, casual employment) in disability support, aged care or similar roles preferred. 
•	Valid Driver's License , First Aid and CPR certification, police check and Working with Children Check / DHS – DCSI – Disability Employment Screening Clearance / NDIS Worker Check or willing to complete when requested. 
•	Australian Citizen or Permanent Resident Visa holder are encouraged to apply 
•	Excellent organization and team management skills. 
•	Ability to work and blend in a team. 
•	Adhere to industrial compliance requirements. 
•	Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, ability to work independently and as part of a team. 
•	Compassionate, patient, reliable, and respectful. 

What We Offer: 
•	Competitive Salary: Attractive hourly rates and salary packages. 
•	Professional Development: Ongoing training and career advancement opportunities. 
•	Supportive Environment: A welcoming and supportive team culture. 
•	Flexibility: Flexible working hours to suit your lifestyle. 
•	Benefits: Employee assistance programs, health, and wellness initiatives, and more. 

Salary: $72,000/- to $82,000/- per Annum plus superannuation
